findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:127-139 — prune `if: steps.mathlib_ltar_restore.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'`; save `if: ... cache-hit != 'true' && steps.mathlib_ltar_prune.outcome == 'success'`. The workflow comment at ci.yml:120-126 explains this; the doc does not.
findings.fix: State that main publishes only when the restore was not an exact-key hit (the exact key is immutable and already holds this pin's snapshot), and that a failed prune skips publication rather than saving an unpruned snapshot.
findings.issue: "The main `ci.yml` workflow publishes a narrow snapshot" / "Before publishing, main runs `lake exe cache clean`" reads as unconditional, but both the prune and save steps are gated on `cache-hit != 'true'` (ci.yml:129,134) and the save additionally requires `mathlib_ltar_prune.outcome == 'success'`. An operator wondering why a main run did not refresh the snapshot is misled.

findings.evidence: grep: `.github/workflows/pages.yml:208,281` and `.github/workflows/pr-profile.yml:319,419` run `lake exe cache get`; `MATHLIB_CACHE_DIR` appears only in ci.yml:30 and pr-build.yml:64.
findings.fix: Add one sentence naming `pages.yml` and `pr-profile.yml` as intentionally outside this cache (they still fetch from Mathlib's server into the default `~/.cache/mathlib`), and why.
findings.issue: The section describes the `.ltar` cache as the Mathlib download cache for the project ("which knob feeds which workflow"), but `pages.yml` and `pr-profile.yml` also run `lake exe cache get` and set no `MATHLIB_CACHE_DIR`, so they neither restore nor share this store. The PR description calls this a deliberate rollout control; nothing in the doc records it.

summary: Workflow comments are accurate and well-sourced, but the new docs/cache-infrastructure.md section describes main's publication as unconditional when it is skipped on an exact-key restore (and on a prune failure), and it presents the .ltar store as the project-wide Mathlib download cache while pages.yml and pr-profile.yml are deliberately left out.
